brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.requirement: Compact desk unit with a drawer
requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases (0,0), (1,-1), (1,0) form a compact cluster. A notch drawer frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm, notch:0#0,-1#notch5) fills the empty position at (0,-1) between two bases, giving a drawer as wide as that position allows. Joint bolts at (1,-1) and (1,0) lock the cluster. check_build: no errors, no loose-body warnings, meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet, to hold a small platform
requirements.evidence: Mount spike spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0 sits at the junction where bases (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0) meet, with platform-sm (small platform) set as its accessory. A solid spike refused the platform (TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED), so the mount variant was used. The platform was not visible in get_build output, so its presence rests on the setSpikeAccessory success response.

finish.summary: Built a three-base compact unit (full bases at (0,0), (1,-1), (1,0)) with a notch drawer frame at (0,-1), joint bolts locking the cluster, and a mount spike at the three-base corner carrying a small platform. check_build is clean (no errors, meshClash clear), with only an informational cap-face note. No strength claims are made.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
